<span data-as="p">Ultracode runs the session at <code>xhigh</code> effort and takes precedence over <code>effortLevel</code> and <a class="link" href="#modelsettings"><code>modelSettings</code></a> entries. If an <a class="link" href="/docs/en/model-config#organization-effort-limits">effort cap</a> below <code>xhigh</code> applies to the model, such as a <a class="link" href="#maxeffortlevel"><code>maxEffortLevel</code></a> setting, the session runs at the cap instead and ultracode stays off. Claude then doesn’t plan workflows on its own, and <code>/effort</code> doesn’t offer <code>ultracode</code>. An Agent SDK <code>apply_flag_settings</code> control request also accepts the key.</span>
<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="permission-settings"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#permission-settings">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Permission settings</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">Decide what Claude can do without asking, which permission mode a session starts in, and what auto mode’s classifier allows. For rule syntax and the permission model, see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions">Configure permissions</a>.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="allowmanagedpermissionrulesonly"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#allowmanagedpermissionrulesonly">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Make managed settings the only settings source of permission rules. Claude Code then ignores <code>allow</code>, <code>ask</code>, and <code>deny</code> rules in user, project, local, and <code>--settings</code> files, ignores <code>--allowedTools</code>, hides the always-allow choices in permission prompts, and stops saving new rules.</span>
<span data-as="p">When <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#let-an-embedding-host-add-policy">parent settings from an embedding host</a> apply, Claude Code treats them as part of the managed tier: it keeps their <code>deny</code> and <code>ask</code> rules and drops their <code>allow</code> rules and <code>additionalDirectories</code>.</span>
<span data-as="p"><code>--disallowedTools</code> rules and the current session’s <code>deny</code> and <code>ask</code> rules still apply, including after Claude Code reloads settings mid-session. They only restrict, so they can’t widen what the managed rules grant. Before v2.1.257, Claude Code dropped those command-line and session rules at the first settings reload.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Managed</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: Boolean<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>true</code>: managed settings become the only settings source of permission rules</li>
<li><code>false</code>: Claude Code applies permission rules from user, project, local, and <code>--settings</code> files in addition to the managed ones</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so Claude Code applies permission rules from user, project, and local settings and from <code>--settings</code>, in addition to the managed ones</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">This key doesn’t lock down the MCP server allowlist; for that, set <a class="link" href="#allowmanagedmcpserversonly"><code>allowManagedMcpServersOnly</code></a>. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#managed-only-settings">Managed-only settings</a>.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="automode"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#automode">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>autoMode</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Add your own rules to what the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permission-modes#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode">auto mode</a> classifier blocks and allows. Use it to tell the classifier which repos, buckets, and domains your organization trusts, so it stops blocking routine internal operations. The classifier ships with <a class="link" href="/docs/en/auto-mode-config#inspect-the-defaults-and-your-effective-config">built-in allow and deny rules</a>. Include the literal string <code>"$defaults"</code> in an array to keep those built-in rules at that position and add yours around them; leave it out to replace them with yours.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>User or managed</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: object with <code>environment</code>, <code>allow</code>, <code>soft_deny</code>, and <code>hard_deny</code> arrays of prose rules, plus the <a class="link" href="#automode-classifyallshell"><code>classifyAllShell</code></a> Boolean</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so the classifier uses only its <a class="link" href="/docs/en/auto-mode-config#inspect-the-defaults-and-your-effective-config">built-in rules</a></li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">This example keeps the built-in <code>soft_deny</code> rules, through <code>"$defaults"</code>, and adds one more that blocks <code>terraform apply</code>:</span>

<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="automode-classifyallshell"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#automode-classifyallshell">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>autoMode.classifyAllShell</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Send every Bash and PowerShell command through the auto mode classifier while auto mode is active. By default, auto mode suspends only allow rules that could run arbitrary code: tool-wide and wildcard rules such as <code>Bash(*)</code>, and interpreter or shell-wrapper prefixes such as <code>Bash(python *)</code>. A command that any other allow rule matches, such as <code>Bash(npm test)</code>, skips the classifier, and a destructive argument the rule’s prefix didn’t anticipate can get through unseen. Setting this key suspends every shell allow rule for the session so the classifier sees every command. Requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>User or managed</code></a>. Read wherever <a class="link" href="#automode"><code>autoMode</code></a> is read.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: Boolean<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>true</code>: while auto mode is active, Claude Code sends every Bash and PowerShell command through the classifier and suspends your shell allow rules; outside auto mode the rules still apply</li>
<li><code>false</code>: auto mode suspends only allow rules that could run arbitrary code, such as <code>Bash(*)</code> and <code>Bash(python *)</code>; a command that any other allow rule matches skips the classifier, and every other shell command goes through it</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: <code>false</code></li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Remove <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permission-modes#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode">auto mode</a> from the <code>Shift+Tab</code> cycle. Any session that would otherwise <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permission-modes#which-mode-a-session-starts-in">start in auto mode</a>, whether from <code>--permission-mode auto</code>, a settings file, or the built-in default, starts in <code>default</code> instead. Administrators set it in managed settings to prevent developers in their organization from using auto mode.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a>. Most useful in <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings">managed settings</a>, where users can’t override it. Also accepted under <code>permissions</code> as <code>permissions.disableAutoMode</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: the string <code>"disable"</code></li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Control which tools Claude can use without asking, which ones always prompt, and which ones are blocked, and set the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permission-modes">permission mode</a> a session starts in. Every <code>permissions.*</code> key below nests under this object.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: object with <code>allow</code>, <code>ask</code>, <code>deny</code>, <code>additionalDirectories</code>, <code>blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories</code>, <code>defaultMode</code>, <code>disableBypassPermissionsMode</code>, and <code>disableAutoMode</code></li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">The three rule arrays share one syntax; see <a class="link" href="#permission-rule-syntax">Permission rule syntax</a> under <code>permissions.allow</code>. For how permission rules from different files combine, see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#settings-precedence">how permission rules merge across scopes</a>; for how settings keys in general combine, see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings#settings-precedence">Settings precedence</a> on the settings guide.</span>

<span data-as="p">Choose whether Claude Code uses the auto mode classifier to review shell commands in plan mode. With the default <code>true</code>, the classifier reviews each command during planning when auto mode is available and you see no prompt. Set <code>false</code> to get a permission prompt for every command outside the built-in read-only set. Appears in <code>/config</code> as <strong>Use auto mode during plan</strong>.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>User, local, or managed</code></a>. A repository can’t turn it off for you.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: Boolean<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>true</code>: the same as unset; when auto mode is available, the classifier reviews each shell command during planning instead of prompting you for it. A <code>false</code> in any of these files still turns it off</li>
<li><code>false</code>: you get a permission prompt for every command outside the built-in read-only set</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: <code>true</code></li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">List the tool uses Claude Code approves without asking you. In an MCP rule, <code>*</code> can appear only in the tool name after the <code>mcp__&lt;server&gt;__</code> prefix, such as <code>mcp__github__get_*</code>; it can’t appear in the server name.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: array of permission rule strings</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset</li>
<li><strong>Per-session overrides</strong>: <code>--allowedTools</code> adds allow rules for one session, and a deny rule from any settings file still blocks a tool it names</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">This example approves <code>git diff</code> and lets Claude Code read your <code>.zshrc</code> without asking:</span>

<span data-as="p">Claude Code applies <code>allow</code> rules from a project’s <code>.claude/settings.json</code> only after you accept the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#project-allow-rules-and-workspace-trust">workspace trust dialog</a> for that folder.</span>
<h4 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="permission-rule-syntax"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#permission-rule-syntax">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Permission rule syntax</span></h4>
<span data-as="p">Permission rules follow the format <code>Tool</code> or <code>Tool(specifier)</code>. Claude Code evaluates <code>deny</code> rules first, then <code>ask</code>, then <code>allow</code>, and the first match decides regardless of how specific each rule is; see the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#manage-permissions">permission rule evaluation order</a>.</span>
<span data-as="p">Each row shows one rule shape and what it matches.</span>
<!-- --><div class="min-w-0 [--page-padding:20px] flex w-[calc(100%+(var(--page-padding)*2))] my-[1em] py-[1em] -mx-(--page-padding) max-w-none [contain:inline-size]" data-component-part="scroll-area" data-table-wrapper="true" role="presentation" style="position:relative;--scroll-area-corner-height:0px;--scroll-area-corner-width:0px"><div aria-label="Scrollable table" class="size-full rounded-[inherit] [--scroll-area-fade-size:32px] overflow-y-hidden! base-ui-disable-scrollbar" data-component-part="scroll-area-viewport" data-id="base-ui-_R_1gsllktbsnlhjiuqsnpfiutb_-viewport" role="region" style="overflow:scroll" tabindex="-1"><div class="flex" data-component-part="scroll-area-content" role="presentation" style="min-width:fit-content"><div class="px-(--page-padding) grow max-w-none table"><table class="m-0 min-w-full w-full max-w-none table [&amp;_th]:text-left [&amp;_td[data-numeric]]:tabular-nums [&amp;_td]:min-w-[150px]"><thead><tr><th style="text-align:left">Rule</th><th style="text-align:left">What it matches</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>Bash</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Every Bash command</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>Bash(npm run *)</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Commands starting with <code>npm run</code></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>Read(./.env)</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Reads of the <code>.env</code> file</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>WebFetch(domain:example.com)</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Fetch requests to example.com</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>
<span data-as="p">For the complete rule syntax, including wildcard behavior, tool-specific patterns for Read, Edit, WebFetch, MCP, and Agent rules, and the security limitations of Bash patterns, see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#permission-rule-syntax">Permission rule syntax</a>.</span>

<span data-as="p">List the tool uses that prompt you for confirmation even in a permission mode that would otherwise approve them, such as <code>acceptEdits</code> or <code>bypassPermissions</code>. In <code>dontAsk</code> mode Claude Code denies a matching tool use instead of prompting.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: array of permission rule strings</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset</li>
</ul>

<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="permissions-deny"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#permissions-deny">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>permissions.deny</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">List the tool uses Claude Code blocks. Use it for files that hold API keys, secrets, or environment values: Claude Code excludes matching files from file discovery and search results, denies reads of them, and blocks the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#read-and-edit">Edit and Write tools</a> on the matching paths. Read and Edit deny rules apply to Claude’s built-in file tools, to file commands Claude Code recognizes in Bash, such as <code>cat</code>, <code>head</code>, <code>tail</code>, and <code>sed</code>, and to the targets of Bash <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#redirections">redirections</a> such as <code>&gt; file</code> and <code>&lt; file</code>; they don’t apply to a command that reads files without naming them, such as <code>grep -r pattern .</code>, or to arbitrary subprocesses, so for OS-level enforcement <a class="link" href="/docs/en/sandboxing">enable the sandbox</a>.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: array of permission rule strings</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset</li>
<li><strong>Per-session overrides</strong>: <code>--disallowedTools</code> adds deny rules for one session alongside this key</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Tool names accept glob patterns, so <code>"*"</code> denies every tool and <code>"mcp__*"</code> denies every MCP tool. Claude Code ignores a deny rule for the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/tools-reference#endconversation-tool-behavior"><code>EndConversation</code></a> tool as long as any other tool is still available to Claude. A <code>Bash</code> deny rule matches the command as Claude writes it, so <code>Bash(curl *)</code> doesn’t stop <code>/usr/bin/curl</code> or <code>sh -c 'curl …'</code>; see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#bash-rule-limits">what a Bash rule doesn’t match</a>. This key replaces the deprecated <code>ignorePatterns</code> configuration.</span>

<span data-as="p">Give Claude file access to directories outside the one you started in, as additional <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#working-directories">working directories</a>. Most <code>.claude/</code> configuration is <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#additional-directories-grant-file-access-not-configuration">not discovered</a> from these directories.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: array of directory paths</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset</li>
<li><strong>Per-session overrides</strong>: <code>--add-dir</code> and <code>/add-dir</code> add directories for one session alongside this key</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Like <code>allow</code> rules, entries in a project’s <code>.claude/settings.json</code> take effect only after you accept the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#project-allow-rules-and-workspace-trust">workspace trust dialog</a> for that folder.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="permissions-blockreadsoutsideworkingdirectories"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#permissions-blockreadsoutsideworkingdirectories">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Stop Claude from reading paths outside the session’s <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#working-directories">working directories</a> with the Read, Grep, Glob, and LSP tools, in every permission mode including <code>bypassPermissions</code>. A Bash command that reads a matching path through a file command Claude Code recognizes, such as <code>cat</code>, prompts you even in auto mode and <code>bypassPermissions</code> mode. Requires Claude Code v2.1.257 or later.</span>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code also writes <code>true</code> here when you choose to block such reads on <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permission-modes#first-read-outside-the-working-directories">auto mode’s prompt before the first read outside the working directories</a>.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a>. If any settings source sets <code>true</code>, the block applies, so a repository’s checked-in file can turn the block on for a project but can’t lift a block you set.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: Boolean<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>true</code>: file reads outside the working directories are blocked</li>
<li><code>false</code>: the same as unset; a <code>true</code> in any other settings file still blocks</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so reads outside the working directories follow your permission mode and rules</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">If only a repository’s checked-in settings file adds a directory, the block still applies to reads there. Files Claude Code itself needs stay readable, such as your skills, plugins, rules, agents, commands, and the <code>CLAUDE.md</code> memory file under <code>~/.claude/</code>.</span>
<span data-as="p">When the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/sandboxing">sandbox</a> is on, the block also denies sandboxed commands read access to home directories and mounted-volume roots outside the working directories. A retry that needs approval to <a class="link" href="/docs/en/sandboxing#the-unsandboxed-retry-escape-hatch">run outside the sandbox</a> prompts you even in <code>bypassPermissions</code> mode. Files a tool reads from your home directory, such as <code>~/.gitconfig</code>, are denied with the rest; re-open a specific path with <a class="link" href="#sandbox-filesystem-allowread"><code>sandbox.filesystem.allowRead</code></a> when a tool needs it.</span>
<span data-as="p">When the session’s working directory is a linked <a class="link" href="/docs/en/worktrees">git worktree</a>, including one Claude Code entered mid-session, the repository’s common <code>.git</code> directory stays readable and writable to sandboxed commands, so git keeps working there.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="permissions-defaultmode"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#permissions-defaultmode">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>permissions.defaultMode</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Set the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permission-modes">permission mode</a> new sessions start in. When you leave it unset, sessions start in the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permission-modes#which-mode-a-session-starts-in">built-in default</a> for your plan and surface.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a>. <code>auto</code> and <code>bypassPermissions</code> don’t take effect from project or local settings, so set them in <code>~/.claude/settings.json</code> instead. Before v2.1.257, <code>bypassPermissions</code> took effect from any file. For conversations the VS Code extension starts, Claude Code reads only user, managed, and <code>--settings</code> values.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: string, one of:<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>"default"</code>: Claude Code runs only reads without asking</li>
<li><code>"acceptEdits"</code>: Claude Code also runs file edits and common filesystem commands such as <code>mkdir</code> and <code>mv</code> without asking</li>
<li><code>"plan"</code>: Claude Code reads and plans but blocks edits until you approve a plan</li>
<li><code>"auto"</code>: Claude Code runs everything, with background safety checks</li>
<li><code>"dontAsk"</code>: Claude Code runs only pre-approved tools and auto-denies every call that would otherwise prompt</li>
<li><code>"bypassPermissions"</code>: Claude Code runs everything without asking</li>
<li><code>"manual"</code>: an alias for <code>"default"</code>, in Claude Code v2.1.200 or later</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset</li>
<li><strong>Per-session overrides</strong>: <code>--permission-mode</code>, and its equivalent <code>--dangerously-skip-permissions</code> for <code>bypassPermissions</code>, take precedence over this key for one session</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Permission rules layer on top of every mode: <code>deny</code> rules block in every mode, including <code>bypassPermissions</code>. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permission-modes">Permission modes</a>. <code>manual</code> names the permission mode labeled Manual in the CLI and the VS Code extension; the alias requires Claude Code v2.1.200 or later. In Claude Code on the web, Claude Code honors only <code>acceptEdits</code>, <code>plan</code>, <code>default</code>, and <code>auto</code> from this key. For conversations the VS Code extension starts, see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permission-modes#switch-permission-modes">which setting the extension reads for the starting permission mode</a>.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="permissions-disablebypasspermissionsmode"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#permissions-disablebypasspermissionsmode">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Prevent anyone from entering <code>bypassPermissions</code> mode. Claude Code then rejects the <code>--dangerously-skip-permissions</code> flag, and ignores an <a class="link" href="/docs/en/sub-agents#permission-modes">agent definition’s</a> <code>permissionMode: bypassPermissions</code>, so the subagent runs with the parent session’s permission mode.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a>. Typically set in <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings">managed settings</a> to enforce organizational policy.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: the string <code>"disable"</code></li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset</li>
<li><strong>Per-session overrides</strong>: this key takes precedence over <code>--dangerously-skip-permissions</code>, which Claude Code rejects while the key is set</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Before v2.1.223, Claude Code applied the frontmatter permission mode even with bypass disabled.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="skipautopermissionprompt"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#skipautopermissionprompt">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>skipAutoPermissionPrompt</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Skip the one-time notice describing <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permission-modes#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode">auto mode</a> that Claude Code shows when you first enter auto mode yourself, for example through your own settings or the mode selector, rather than when the built-in default starts a session in it. Claude Code shows that notice once and then records that it was shown, so this key only matters where the notice hasn’t appeared yet.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>User or managed</code></a>. A repository can’t set it for you.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: Boolean<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>true</code>: Claude Code skips the notice</li>
<li><code>false</code>: the same as unset; the notice appears once unless another of these files sets <code>true</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so the notice appears once</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Skip the confirmation dialog Claude Code shows before a session enters <code>bypassPermissions</code> mode, whether from <code>--dangerously-skip-permissions</code> or from <code>defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"</code>. Claude Code writes <code>true</code> here in your user settings when you accept that dialog once.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>User, local, or managed</code></a>. An untrusted repository can’t skip the dialog for you.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: Boolean<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>true</code>: Claude Code skips the confirmation dialog before a session enters <code>bypassPermissions</code> mode</li>
<li><code>false</code>: the same as unset; the dialog appears unless another of these files sets <code>true</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so the dialog appears</li>
</ul>

<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="sandbox-settings"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#sandbox-settings">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Sandbox settings</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">Isolate the commands Claude runs from your filesystem, your network, and your credentials. For how sandboxing works and platform requirements, see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/sandboxing">Sandboxing</a>.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="sandbox"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#sandbox">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>sandbox</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Isolate the Bash commands Claude runs from your filesystem and network with <a class="link" href="/docs/en/sandboxing">sandboxing</a>. Turn the sandbox on with <code>enabled</code>, then narrow or widen what sandboxed commands can touch with the <code>filesystem</code>, <code>network</code>, and <code>credentials</code> sub-objects. The sandbox runs on macOS, Linux, and WSL2.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: object with <code>enabled</code>, <code>failIfUnavailable</code>, <code>autoAllowBashIfSandboxed</code>, <code>excludedCommands</code>, <code>allowUnsandboxedCommands</code>, <code>enableWeakerNestedSandbox</code>, <code>enableWeakerNetworkIsolation</code>, <code>allowAppleEvents</code>, <code>bwrapPath</code>, <code>socatPath</code>, <code>ignoreViolations</code>, and <code>ripgrep</code>, plus the <code>filesystem</code>, <code>network</code>, and <code>credentials</code> objects</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so Claude Code runs commands without a sandbox</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">This turns the sandbox on, skips permission prompts for sandboxed commands, runs <code>docker</code> outside the sandbox, opens two extra write paths, hides your AWS credentials file, and pre-allows GitHub and npm:</span>

<span data-as="p">Claude Code takes a Boolean key’s value from the highest-precedence settings scope that sets it, so a managed <code>enabled</code> or <code>failIfUnavailable</code> overrides anything a developer sets. It merges array keys across every settings scope the session loads, so a developer can append entries; see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/sandboxing#keep-developers-from-widening-the-policy">Keep developers from widening the policy</a> for the managed-only locks. To require the sandbox for an organization, see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/sandboxing#enforce-sandboxing-with-managed-settings">Enforce sandboxing with managed settings</a>.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="sandbox-enabled"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#sandbox-enabled">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>sandbox.enabled</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Turn on <a class="link" href="/docs/en/sandboxing">sandboxing</a> for Bash commands. When you pick a mode in the <code>/sandbox</code> panel, Claude Code writes this key to <code>.claude/settings.local.json</code> for the current project; set it in <code>~/.claude/settings.json</code> to sandbox every project.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: Boolean<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>true</code>: Claude Code sandboxes Bash commands</li>
<li><code>false</code>: Bash commands run unsandboxed</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: <code>false</code></li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">On Linux and WSL2 the sandbox needs <code>bubblewrap</code> and <code>socat</code>; see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/sandboxing#set-up-linux-and-wsl2">Set up Linux and WSL2</a>. When the sandbox can’t start, Claude Code shows a warning and runs commands unsandboxed unless you also set <a class="link" href="#sandbox-failifunavailable"><code>failIfUnavailable</code></a>.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="sandbox-failifunavailable"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#sandbox-failifunavailable">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>sandbox.failIfUnavailable</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Make Claude Code exit with an error at startup when <code>sandbox.enabled</code> is <code>true</code> but the sandbox can’t start, because a dependency is missing or the platform is unsupported. Without it, Claude Code shows a warning and runs commands unsandboxed. Use it in managed settings when your organization requires sandboxing as a hard gate.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: Boolean<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>true</code>: Claude Code exits with an error at startup when <code>sandbox.enabled</code> is <code>true</code> but the sandbox can’t start</li>
<li><code>false</code>: Claude Code shows a warning and runs commands unsandboxed</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: <code>false</code></li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">This makes every managed machine sandbox commands or refuse to start:</span>

<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="sandbox-autoallowbashifsandboxed"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#sandbox-autoallowbashifsandboxed">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Let Claude Code run sandboxed Bash commands without a permission prompt. Commands that can’t run in the sandbox still go through the regular permission flow, and <code>deny</code> rules and content-scoped <code>ask</code> rules such as <code>Bash(git push *)</code> still apply; a bare <code>Bash</code> ask rule is skipped for sandboxed commands. Set it to <code>false</code> to send sandboxed commands through the regular permission flow too, which the <code>/sandbox</code> <strong>Mode</strong> tab calls regular permissions mode.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: Boolean<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>true</code>: Claude Code runs sandboxed Bash commands without a permission prompt, subject to <code>deny</code> rules and content-scoped <code>ask</code> rules; <code>CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB</code> turns auto-allow off</li>
<li><code>false</code>: sandboxed commands go through the regular permission flow, so your allow rules and permission mode decide. The <code>/sandbox</code> <strong>Mode</strong> tab calls this regular permissions mode</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: <code>true</code></li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">This keeps the sandbox on and sends sandboxed commands through the regular permission flow:</span>

<span data-as="p">Name commands that Claude Code always runs outside the sandbox, such as tools that don’t work under it. Each entry uses the same syntax as the content of a <code>Bash(...)</code> <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#permission-rule-syntax">permission rule</a>: an exact command, a prefix such as <code>docker *</code>, or a wildcard pattern. When any part of a compound command matches an entry, Claude Code runs the whole command unsandboxed.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: array of command patterns</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so no command is excluded</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Excluded commands still go through the regular permission flow. Exclusion is a convenience, not a security boundary: prefer <a class="link" href="#sandbox-filesystem-allowwrite"><code>filesystem.allowWrite</code></a> when a tool only needs to write somewhere specific. Claude Code merges entries across every settings scope the session loads, and there is no managed-only lock for this list, so keep a managed list narrow.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="sandbox-allowunsandboxedcommands"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#sandbox-allowunsandboxedcommands">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Let Claude retry a command outside the sandbox with the <code>dangerouslyDisableSandbox</code> parameter after the sandbox blocks it. Set it to <code>false</code> so Claude Code ignores that parameter completely and every command Claude runs must be sandboxed or appear in <a class="link" href="#sandbox-excludedcommands"><code>excludedCommands</code></a>. The <code>/sandbox</code> <strong>Overrides</strong> tab shows that state as <strong>Strict sandbox mode</strong>. Use <code>false</code> in managed settings for policies that require strict sandboxing.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: Boolean<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>true</code>: Claude can retry a command outside the sandbox with the <code>dangerouslyDisableSandbox</code> parameter after the sandbox blocks it</li>
<li><code>false</code>: Claude Code ignores that parameter, so every command Claude runs is sandboxed or appears in <code>excludedCommands</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: <code>true</code></li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">This enforces strict sandbox mode for everyone the managed settings cover:</span>

<span data-as="p">An unsandboxed retry goes through the regular permission flow, with a prompt in Manual mode. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/sandboxing#the-unsandboxed-retry-escape-hatch">The unsandboxed retry escape hatch</a>.</span>
<span data-as="p">To see when commands you type yourself at the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/interactive-mode#shell-mode-with-prefix"><code>!</code> shell-mode prompt</a> run sandboxed, see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/sandboxing#the-unsandboxed-retry-escape-hatch">strict sandbox mode</a>.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="sandbox-filesystem"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#sandbox-filesystem">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>sandbox.filesystem</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Control which paths sandboxed commands can read and write. By default they can write to the working directory, the session temp directory, and directories you add with <code>--add-dir</code>, <code>/add-dir</code>, or <code>permissions.additionalDirectories</code>, and can read the rest of the filesystem, including credential files. Widen or narrow that with the four path lists, or switch the filesystem layer off with <code>disabled</code>. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/sandboxing#filesystem-isolation">Filesystem isolation</a> for the default boundaries.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: object with <code>allowWrite</code>, <code>denyWrite</code>, <code>denyRead</code>, and <code>allowRead</code> arrays, plus the <code>allowManagedReadPathsOnly</code> and <code>disabled</code> Booleans</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so the default read and write boundaries apply</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">This lets sandboxed commands write to a build directory and your kubeconfig, and hides your AWS credentials file:</span>

<span class="line"><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">    }</span></span>

</code></pre></div></div></div></div><div aria-hidden="true" class="code-block-fade-overlay print:hidden" data-fade-overlay="true" style="--fade-color-light:#ffffff;--fade-color-dark:#0B0C0E"></div></div>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code enforces these lists at the OS sandbox boundary, so they apply to every subprocess a sandboxed command starts, such as <code>kubectl</code>, <code>terraform</code>, or <code>npm</code>, not only to Claude’s file tools. Claude Code adds your <a class="link" href="/docs/en/sandboxing#permission-rules">permission rules</a> to the same lists: <code>Edit</code> allow and deny rules to <code>allowWrite</code> and <code>denyWrite</code>, <code>Read</code> deny rules to <code>denyRead</code>, and <code>WebFetch(domain:...)</code> allow and deny rules to the <a class="link" href="#sandbox-network"><code>network</code></a> domain lists.</span>
<span data-as="p">Unless a managed-only lock is set, Claude Code merges every list across the settings files the session loads. <a class="link" href="#sandbox-filesystem-allowmanagedreadpathsonly"><code>allowManagedReadPathsOnly</code></a> limits <code>allowRead</code> to entries from managed settings, and <a class="link" href="#sandbox-network-allowmanageddomainsonly"><code>allowManagedDomainsOnly</code></a> does the same for allowed domains.</span>
<span data-as="p"><a class="link" href="/docs/en/sandboxing#configure-sandboxing">Configure sandboxing</a> covers sources you exclude with <code>--setting-sources</code>. When you edit a list during a session, Claude Code <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings#when-edits-take-effect">applies the change to the running session</a>.</span>
<h4 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="sandbox-path-prefixes"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#sandbox-path-prefixes">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Sandbox path prefixes</span></h4>
<span data-as="p">Paths in <code>allowWrite</code>, <code>denyWrite</code>, <code>denyRead</code>, <code>allowRead</code>, and <a class="link" href="#sandbox-credentials-files"><code>credentials.files</code></a> resolve by their prefix:</span>
<!-- --><div class="min-w-0 [--page-padding:20px] flex w-[calc(100%+(var(--page-padding)*2))] my-[1em] py-[1em] -mx-(--page-padding) max-w-none [contain:inline-size]" data-component-part="scroll-area" data-table-wrapper="true" role="presentation" style="position:relative;--scroll-area-corner-height:0px;--scroll-area-corner-width:0px"><div aria-label="Scrollable table" class="size-full rounded-[inherit] [--scroll-area-fade-size:32px] overflow-y-hidden! base-ui-disable-scrollbar" data-component-part="scroll-area-viewport" data-id="base-ui-_R_27kllktbsnlhjiuqsnpfiutb_-viewport" role="region" style="overflow:scroll" tabindex="-1"><div class="flex" data-component-part="scroll-area-content" role="presentation" style="min-width:fit-content"><div class="px-(--page-padding) grow max-w-none table"><table class="m-0 min-w-full w-full max-w-none table [&amp;_th]:text-left [&amp;_td[data-numeric]]:tabular-nums [&amp;_td]:min-w-[150px]"><thead><tr><th style="text-align:left">Prefix</th><th style="text-align:left">Meaning</th><th style="text-align:left">Example</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td data-numeric="true" style="text-align:left"><code>/</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Absolute path from filesystem root</td><td style="text-align:left"><code>/tmp/build</code> stays <code>/tmp/build</code></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>~/</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Relative to home directory</td><td style="text-align:left"><code>~/.kube</code> becomes <code>$HOME/.kube</code></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>./</code> or no prefix</td><td style="text-align:left">Relative to the project root for project settings, or to <code>~/.claude</code> for user settings</td><td style="text-align:left"><code>./output</code> in <code>.claude/settings.json</code> resolves to <code>&lt;project-root&gt;/output</code></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>
<span data-as="p">The <code>//path</code> prefix for absolute paths also works. If you use single-slash <code>/path</code> expecting project-relative resolution, switch to <code>./path</code>. This syntax differs from <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#read-and-edit">Read and Edit permission rules</a>, which use <code>//path</code> for absolute and <code>/path</code> for project-relative: sandbox filesystem paths use standard conventions, so <code>/tmp/build</code> is an absolute path.</span>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code strips a trailing slash from a directory path, so <code>~/.aws</code> and <code>~/.aws/</code> match the same directory. Before v2.1.224, Claude Code passed the trailing slash through to the sandbox, and Claude could still read or write paths under a <code>denyRead</code> or <code>denyWrite</code> entry written with one.</span>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code also removes a trailing <code>/**</code>, so <code>~/build/**</code> and <code>~/build</code> cover the same directory. Whether a wildcard such as <code>*</code> works depends on which list the entry is in and on the platform:</span>
<ul>
<li><strong><code>allowWrite</code> and <code>denyWrite</code></strong>: on macOS, wildcards work. On Linux and WSL2, the sandbox mounts concrete paths, so Claude Code skips an entry that contains <code>*</code>, <code>?</code>, or <code>[</code> once the trailing <code>/**</code> is removed, and that entry has no effect. Claude Code adds the paths from your <code>Edit</code> permission rules to these lists, so the same limit applies to them, and the <strong>Config</strong> tab of <code>/sandbox</code> warns about <code>Edit</code> and <code>Read</code> permission rules that contain wildcards.</li>
<li><strong><code>denyRead</code> and <code>allowRead</code></strong>: wildcards work on every platform. On Linux and WSL2, Claude Code expands a read entry to the concrete paths it matches, which it doesn’t do for the write lists.</li>
</ul>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="sandbox-filesystem-allowwrite"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#sandbox-filesystem-allowwrite">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Add paths where sandboxed commands can write, beyond the working directory, the session temp directory, and the directories you’ve added with <code>--add-dir</code>, <code>/add-dir</code>, or <code>permissions.additionalDirectories</code>. Use it when a subprocess such as <code>kubectl</code> or a build tool needs to write outside the project.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: array of path strings, using the <a class="link" href="#sandbox-path-prefixes">sandbox path prefixes</a></li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so sandboxed commands can write to the working directory, the session temp directory, directories you’ve added with <code>--add-dir</code> or <code>/add-dir</code>, and directories in <a class="link" href="#permissions-additionaldirectories"><code>permissions.additionalDirectories</code></a></li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">This lets a build write under <code>/tmp/build</code> and lets <code>kubectl</code> update your kubeconfig:</span>

<span data-as="p">Claude Code merges entries across every settings scope the session loads: user, project, local, and managed paths combine rather than replace each other, and Claude Code adds the paths from your <code>Edit(...)</code> allow permission rules. An <code>allowWrite</code> entry can’t lift a <a class="link" href="/docs/en/sandboxing#protected-paths">protected path</a>.</span>

<span data-as="p">Block sandboxed commands from writing to specific paths, including paths inside a directory that is otherwise writable.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: array of path strings, using the <a class="link" href="#sandbox-path-prefixes">sandbox path prefixes</a></li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">This keeps sandboxed commands from changing system configuration or installing binaries:</span>

<span data-as="p">Block sandboxed commands from reading specific paths, such as credential files that the default read policy would otherwise expose. To protect a credential file and keep it usable through the sandbox proxy, see <a class="link" href="#sandbox-credentials"><code>sandbox.credentials</code></a> instead.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: array of path strings, using the <a class="link" href="#sandbox-path-prefixes">sandbox path prefixes</a></li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so sandboxed commands keep the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/sandboxing#filesystem-isolation">default read access</a>, which includes credential files such as <code>~/.aws/credentials</code></li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Claude Code merges entries across every settings scope the session loads, and adds the paths from your <code>Read(...)</code> deny permission rules. When <a class="link" href="#sandbox-filesystem-disabled"><code>filesystem.disabled</code></a> is <code>true</code>, Claude Code doesn’t enforce these entries.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="sandbox-filesystem-allowread"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#sandbox-filesystem-allowread">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>sandbox.filesystem.allowRead</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Re-open reading for specific paths inside a region that <a class="link" href="#sandbox-filesystem-denyread"><code>denyRead</code></a> blocks, to build workspace-only read access. An exact or wildcard <code>denyRead</code> entry stays blocked inside a broader <code>allowRead</code>, as the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/sandboxing#configure-sandboxing">overlap table</a> shows. When a wildcard <code>denyRead</code> entry such as <code>~/**/.env</code> matches a directory, Claude Code blocks reads of its contents as well. Before v2.1.236 on macOS, Claude Code re-opened the paths a wildcard <code>denyRead</code> entry matched wherever a broader <code>allowRead</code> entry covered them, and left a matched directory’s contents readable.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: array of path strings, using the <a class="link" href="#sandbox-path-prefixes">sandbox path prefixes</a></li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset</li>
</ul>
