<span data-as="p">Unlike <a class="link" href="#awsauthrefresh"><code>awsAuthRefresh</code></a>, Claude Code always runs this command when it’s set, without checking the ambient credentials first. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/amazon-bedrock#advanced-credential-configuration">advanced credential configuration</a>.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="forceloginmethod"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#forceloginmethod">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>forceLoginMethod</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Restrict which kind of account people can log in with. Set <code>"claudeai"</code> to allow only claude.ai accounts, <code>"console"</code> to allow only Claude Console accounts, or <code>"gateway"</code> to send people to a <a class="link" href="/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway">cloud gateway</a> instead of a first-party login. Administrators set it in managed settings and pair it with <a class="link" href="#forceloginorguuid"><code>forceLoginOrgUUID</code></a> to keep developers’ claude.ai logins inside one organization. If you set it to <code>"claudeai"</code> or <code>"console"</code> in any settings file, Claude Code also stops offering the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/authentication#sign-in-without-an-api-key">keyless Console sign-in</a> in the sessions that file applies to.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a>. Claude Code honors <code>"gateway"</code> only from a managed source on the machine: <code>managed-settings.json</code>, the macOS plist or Windows HKLM registry, or a policy helper. It treats <code>"gateway"</code> as unset in user, project, local, HKCU, and server-managed settings, the same rule as <a class="link" href="#forcelogingatewayurl"><code>forceLoginGatewayUrl</code></a>.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: string, one of:<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>"claudeai"</code>: only claude.ai accounts can log in</li>
<li><code>"console"</code>: only Claude Console accounts can log in</li>
<li><code>"gateway"</code>: Claude Code sends people to a cloud gateway instead of a first-party login</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so people pick a login method</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Every first-party login path applies the restriction, including the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/vs-code">VS Code extension</a>, the Agent SDK, <code>claude setup-token</code>, and <code>/install-github-app</code>, except the terminal’s interactive login screen, reached by <code>/login</code> or first-run onboarding, which pre-selects the method without enforcing it. Before v2.1.212, only terminal logins applied it. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/authentication#restrict-login-to-your-organization">Restrict login to your organization</a> for how each login path, environment credentials, and third-party providers are handled.</span>
<span data-as="p">When a managed source on the machine sets <code>"gateway"</code>, Claude Code doesn’t use a leftover login, API key, or <code>apiKeyHelper</code> credential. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/errors#administrator-policy-requires-a-cloud-gateway-sign-in">Administrator policy requires a Cloud gateway sign-in</a> for the message each one produces. If you select a cloud provider through <code>CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK</code> or a similar environment variable, the session doesn’t need the gateway sign-in. Before v2.1.261, Claude Code used a leftover login on these machines.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="forcelogingatewayurl"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#forcelogingatewayurl">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>forceLoginGatewayUrl</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Set the gateway URL the <code>/login</code> Cloud gateway screen connects to, so people reach your <a class="link" href="/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway">cloud gateway</a> without typing its address. The screen has no URL field: with this key set, it shows your gateway URL and connects when the person presses Enter; without it, it tells them to contact their IT administrator.</span>
<span data-as="p">Either this key or <code>forceLoginMethod: "gateway"</code> makes the machine gateway-only, so <code>/login</code> opens on the Cloud gateway screen with no login-method picker. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/errors#administrator-policy-requires-a-cloud-gateway-sign-in">Administrator policy requires a Cloud gateway sign-in</a> for what happens to a leftover first-party login or API key. Set both keys so the screen connects instead of showing an error.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Managed</code></a>. Read only from a source on the machine: <code>managed-settings.json</code>, the macOS plist or Windows HKLM registry, or a policy helper. Claude Code ignores it in HKCU and server-managed settings.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: string, a full URL including the scheme</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so the Cloud gateway screen shows an error telling people to contact their IT administrator</li>
</ul>

<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="forceloginorguuid"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#forceloginorguuid">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>forceLoginOrgUUID</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">From a managed source, require claude.ai account logins to belong to one Anthropic organization, given as a single UUID, or to any of several organizations, given as an array. From any settings file, Claude Code also uses a single UUID to pre-select that organization during a claude.ai or Claude Console login, and pre-selects nothing for an array. If you set the key in any settings file, Claude Code also stops offering the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/authentication#sign-in-without-an-api-key">keyless Console sign-in</a> in the sessions that file applies to and creates an API key instead.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a>. Only a managed source enforces the restriction; a single UUID in any other settings file pre-selects the organization during login without restricting it.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: string, one UUID, or array of strings, several UUIDs</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so any organization can log in</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">This example accepts logins from either of two organizations without pre-selecting one:</span>

<span data-as="p">Run your own command to refresh Google Cloud Application Default Credentials when Claude Code finds they’ve expired or can’t be loaded, so <a class="link" href="/docs/en/google-vertex-ai">Google Cloud’s Agent Platform</a> requests keep working without you re-authenticating by hand.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: string, a shell command line</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so Claude Code’s credential error tells you to run <code>gcloud auth application-default login</code> yourself</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Run your own command to generate the headers Claude Code sends with OpenTelemetry exports, for backends whose tokens rotate. Claude Code runs it at startup and periodically after that, and expects a JSON object of string header values on stdout.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: string, an executable path or a shell command line</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so Claude Code adds no helper-generated headers</li>
</ul>

<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="updates-and-versioning"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#updates-and-versioning">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Updates and versioning</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">Choose an update channel and, for organizations, pin the versions people can run. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/setup#update-claude-code">Update Claude Code</a>.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="autoupdateschannel"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#autoupdateschannel">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>autoUpdatesChannel</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Choose which <a class="link" href="/docs/en/setup#configure-release-channel">release channel</a> background auto-updates and <code>claude update</code> follow. Set <code>"stable"</code> for a version that is typically about one week old and skips releases with major regressions, or <code>"latest"</code> for the most recent release.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a>. Set it in managed settings to enforce one channel across your organization.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: string, one of:<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>"latest"</code>: updates follow the most recent release</li>
<li><code>"stable"</code>: updates follow a version that is typically about one week old and skips releases with major regressions</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so Claude Code follows <code>"latest"</code></li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Claude Code writes <code>"stable"</code> to your user settings when you pick it under <strong>Auto-update channel</strong> in <code>/config</code>, and removes the key when you switch back to latest there. <code>claude install stable</code> and <code>claude install latest</code> also save the channel you name. Switching from <code>"latest"</code> to <code>"stable"</code> in <code>/config</code> asks whether to allow a downgrade or stay on your current version; staying sets <a class="link" href="#minimumversion"><code>minimumVersion</code></a>. Homebrew installs ignore this key: the <code>claude-code</code> cask tracks stable and <code>claude-code@latest</code> tracks latest, and <code>claude update</code> defers to <code>brew upgrade</code>. To turn auto-updates off entirely, set <a class="link" href="/docs/en/setup#disable-auto-updates"><code>DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER</code></a> in <code>env</code>.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="minimumversion"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#minimumversion">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>minimumVersion</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Keep background auto-updates and <code>claude update</code> from installing any version below this one, so moving to the <code>"stable"</code> channel doesn’t downgrade you from a newer <code>"latest"</code> build. Claude Code writes this key for you when you choose to stay on your current version while switching channels in <code>/config</code>, and clears it when you switch back to <code>"latest"</code>.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a>. Set it in managed settings to pin an organization-wide minimum that user and project settings can’t lower.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: string, a version number such as <code>"2.1.100"</code></li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so updates can install any version the channel offers</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">This example follows the stable channel and refuses to install any version below 2.1.100:</span>

<span data-as="p">This key only constrains updates. To make Claude Code refuse to start below a version, use <a class="link" href="#requiredminimumversion"><code>requiredMinimumVersion</code></a> instead. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/setup#pin-a-minimum-version">Pin a minimum version</a>.</span>

<span data-as="p">Set the newest Claude Code version your organization allows to start. When the running version is newer, Claude Code exits at startup and tells the user to install an approved version through your organization’s approved method; <code>claude install &lt;version&gt;</code> may also work. Requires Claude Code v2.1.163 or later.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Managed</code></a>. Claude Code gives no warning when it ignores the key elsewhere.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: string, a version number such as <code>"2.1.150"</code>; a value that isn’t a valid version is ignored</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so no ceiling applies</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Background auto-updates and <code>claude update</code> skip versions above the ceiling, so an installation inside the range stays inside it. <code>claude update</code>, <code>claude install</code>, and <code>claude doctor</code> keep working above the ceiling so users can recover. Pair it with <a class="link" href="#requiredminimumversion"><code>requiredMinimumVersion</code></a> to enforce a range.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="requiredminimumversion"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#requiredminimumversion">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>requiredMinimumVersion</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Set the oldest Claude Code version your organization allows to start. When the running version is older, Claude Code exits at startup and tells the user to update through your organization’s approved method. The check runs at startup only, so a session that’s already running continues. Requires Claude Code v2.1.163 or later.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Managed</code></a>. Claude Code gives no warning when it ignores the key elsewhere.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: string, a version number such as <code>"2.1.150"</code>; a value that isn’t a valid version is ignored</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so no floor applies</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p"><code>claude update</code>, <code>claude install</code>, and <code>claude doctor</code> keep working below the floor so users can recover. Unlike <a class="link" href="#minimumversion"><code>minimumVersion</code></a>, which only prevents downgrades, this key blocks startup. Pair it with <a class="link" href="#requiredmaximumversion"><code>requiredMaximumVersion</code></a> to enforce a range.</span>
<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="tools"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#tools">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer">Tools</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">Turn off specific tools in the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/desktop">Claude Code desktop app</a>. The terminal CLI ignores these keys. For the tools themselves, see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/tools-reference">Tools available to Claude</a>.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="browserexternalpagetools"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#browserexternalpagetools">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>browserExternalPageTools</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Stop Claude from using its tools to read or act on external pages in the desktop app’s <a class="link" href="/docs/en/desktop#browse-external-sites">Browser pane</a>. People in your organization can still open external sites themselves, and local dev server previews keep working with Claude’s tools. The desktop app reads this key; the terminal CLI ignores it.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Managed</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: string, <code>"disabled"</code>; the desktop app also accepts <code>"disable"</code>, in either case</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so Claude’s tools work on external pages</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Any other value leaves Claude’s tools on, and a non-empty string that isn’t one of the two accepted values logs a warning. To block external sites for people and Claude alike, set <a class="link" href="#disablebrowserexternalnavigation"><code>disableBrowserExternalNavigation</code></a> instead. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/desktop#restrict-external-browsing-for-your-organization">Restrict external browsing for your organization</a>.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="disablebrowserexternalnavigation"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#disablebrowserexternalnavigation">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>disableBrowserExternalNavigation</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Turn off external browsing in the desktop app’s <a class="link" href="/docs/en/desktop#browse-external-sites">Browser pane</a> for people and Claude alike. Localhost dev server previews keep working. The desktop app reads this key; the terminal CLI ignores it.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Managed</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: Boolean; only the JSON Boolean <code>true</code> takes effect<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>true</code>: the desktop app turns off external browsing in the Browser pane for people and Claude alike; localhost previews keep working</li>
<li><code>false</code>: external browsing stays on</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so external browsing is on</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">The desktop app ignores any other value, and a value that isn’t a Boolean, such as the string <code>"true"</code> or <code>1</code>, also logs a warning. To leave external browsing on but keep Claude’s tools off external pages, set <a class="link" href="#browserexternalpagetools"><code>browserExternalPageTools</code></a> instead. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/desktop#restrict-external-browsing-for-your-organization">Restrict external browsing for your organization</a>.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="disablemobilesimulatortools"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#disablemobilesimulatortools">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>disableMobileSimulatorTools</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Block Claude’s tools for the desktop app’s <a class="link" href="/docs/en/desktop-ios-simulator#turn-off-simulator-access">iOS Simulator pane</a>. People keep manual use of the pane; only Claude’s access is removed, and nobody can turn it back on from inside the app. The desktop app reads this key; the terminal CLI ignores it.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Managed</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: Boolean; only the JSON Boolean <code>true</code> takes effect<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>true</code>: the desktop app blocks Claude’s tools for the iOS Simulator pane</li>
<li><code>false</code>: Claude’s simulator tools follow each person’s settings toggle in the desktop app</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so Claude’s simulator tools follow each person’s settings toggle in the desktop app</li>
</ul>

<span id="data-and-privacy"></span>
<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="privacy-and-telemetry"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#privacy-and-telemetry">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Privacy and telemetry</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">Control how long Claude Code keeps session data and what it sends. The switches that turn off usage metrics and error reports are environment variables, not settings keys: set <code>DISABLE_TELEMETRY</code>, <code>DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING</code>, or <code>CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC</code> in the <a class="link" href="#env"><code>env</code></a> key or in the shell. <a class="link" href="/docs/en/data-usage#telemetry-services">Telemetry services</a> says what each one stops. Two exceptions turn off from a settings file: <a class="link" href="#feedbackdrafts"><code>feedbackDrafts</code></a> below for Claude-drafted feedback, and <a class="link" href="#feedbacksurveyrate"><code>feedbackSurveyRate</code></a> below for the session survey.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="cleanupperioddays"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#cleanupperioddays">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>cleanupPeriodDays</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Set how many days Claude Code keeps <a class="link" href="/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically">session transcripts and other application data</a> before deleting them. Claude Code runs the deletion as a background sweep after a session starts, as long as it can safely determine the retention period.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: number of days, a whole number, minimum <code>1</code></li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: <code>30</code></li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Set an age limit in days for the transcripts of sessions you started or most recently continued in Claude Desktop or Cowork. Without this key, Claude Code <a class="link" href="/docs/en/claude-directory#cleaned-up-automatically">keeps those transcripts at any age</a>. Claude Code deletes each one once it’s older than both this limit and <a class="link" href="#cleanupperioddays"><code>cleanupPeriodDays</code></a>, so with <code>cleanupPeriodDays</code> at its default of 30, a value of <code>7</code> still keeps them 30 days. When managed settings set <code>cleanupPeriodDays</code>, that period applies instead and this key is ignored. Requires Claude Code v2.1.248 or later.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>User or managed</code></a>. Claude Code also reads the key from a file you pass with <code>--settings</code>, and ignores it in project and local settings.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: number of days, a whole number, minimum <code>0</code></li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: <code>0</code>, which sets no age limit</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Control <a class="link" href="/docs/en/tools-reference#sendfeedback-tool-behavior">Claude-drafted feedback</a>: whether Claude can queue feedback drafts for you to review, and whether Claude Code shows a card when Claude queues one.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>User or managed</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: string, one of <code>"notify"</code>, <code>"quiet"</code>, or <code>"off"</code>
<ul>
<li><code>"notify"</code>: Claude Code shows a card above the prompt when Claude queues a draft, up to <a class="link" href="/docs/en/tools-reference#what-you-see-when-claude-drafts">three cards in a session</a> by default</li>
<li><code>"quiet"</code>: Claude drafts without a card. You see the count of queued drafts in the prompt footer and review them in <code>/feedback</code></li>
<li><code>"off"</code>: Claude Code removes the SendFeedback tool, so Claude can’t queue drafts</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: <code>"notify"</code></li>
<li><strong>Per-session overrides</strong>: <a class="link" href="/docs/en/env-vars"><code>CLAUDE_CODE_SEND_FEEDBACK</code></a> set to <code>0</code> turns the feature off for one session</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Appears in <code>/config</code> as <strong>Claude-drafted feedback</strong>, which writes this key to your user settings. You see the <code>/config</code> row only in sessions <a class="link" href="/docs/en/tools-reference#sessions-without-claude-drafted-feedback">where Claude can draft feedback</a>; setting <code>"off"</code> doesn’t hide it, so you can turn the feature back on from the same row. A value in managed settings takes precedence over your user setting, so when an administrator sets this key, the row shows the managed value and changing it has no effect. Claude Code ignores this key in project and local settings.</span>

<span data-as="p">Set the probability that the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/data-usage#session-quality-surveys">session quality survey</a> appears when a session is eligible for it. Set <code>0</code> to keep the survey from appearing.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: number between <code>0</code> and <code>1</code></li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so Claude Code uses the rate Anthropic sets remotely, or its built-in rate of <code>0.005</code> on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud’s Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry, which don’t receive remote configuration</li>
<li><strong>Per-session overrides</strong>: <a class="link" href="/docs/en/env-vars"><code>CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY</code></a> set to <code>1</code> turns the survey off for one session whatever rate this key sets</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Skip the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/data-usage#webfetch-domain-safety-check">WebFetch domain safety check</a>, which sends each requested hostname to <code>api.anthropic.com</code> before fetching. Set <code>true</code> in environments that block traffic to Anthropic, such as Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud’s Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry deployments with restrictive egress.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Any file</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: Boolean<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>true</code>: Claude Code skips the WebFetch domain safety check</li>
<li><code>false</code>: the check runs before the first fetch to each hostname in a session, and again for a hostname whose earlier check was blocked or failed</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so the check runs before the first fetch to each hostname in a session</li>
</ul>

<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="disablesideloadflags"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#disablesideloadflags">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>disableSideloadFlags</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Reject the <code>--plugin-dir</code>, <code>--plugin-url</code>, <code>--agents</code>, and <code>--mcp-config</code> CLI flags at startup, which users could otherwise pass to bypass <a class="link" href="#strictknownmarketplaces"><code>strictKnownMarketplaces</code></a> for a single run. Claude Code exits with an error naming the rejected flags, and applies the same check to surfaces that start the CLI with these flags internally, currently <a class="link" href="/docs/en/desktop">Cowork</a> local sessions in the desktop app. In <a class="link" href="/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web">cloud sessions</a>, Claude Code drops the MCP servers the server delivered through <code>--mcp-config</code>, other than in-process <code>type: "sdk"</code> entries, and starts the session. Requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Managed</code></a></li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: Boolean<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>true</code>: Claude Code rejects <code>--plugin-dir</code>, <code>--plugin-url</code>, <code>--agents</code>, and <code>--mcp-config</code> at startup and exits with an error naming them, except that in cloud sessions it drops the MCP servers the server delivered through <code>--mcp-config</code>, other than in-process <code>type: "sdk"</code> entries, and starts the session</li>
<li><code>false</code>: Claude Code accepts those flags</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: <code>false</code></li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Claude Code still accepts a <code>--mcp-config</code> whose servers are all in-process <code>type: "sdk"</code> entries, so the Agent SDK and VS Code extension keep working. Users can still add servers with <code>claude mcp add</code> or a <code>.mcp.json</code> file; for per-server control, set <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-mcp"><code>allowedMcpServers</code></a> as well. Requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later.</span>
<span data-as="p">In cloud sessions, Claude Code also ignores server-delivered mid-session MCP updates, the path behind cloud session configuration and SDK <code>setMcpServers()</code> on remote workers. In-process <code>type: "sdk"</code> entries stay exempt there too. Before v2.1.239, a server-delivered <code>--mcp-config</code> blocked a cloud session from starting.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="forceremotesettingsrefresh"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#forceremotesettingsrefresh">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>forceRemoteSettingsRefresh</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Block CLI startup until Claude Code has freshly fetched <a class="link" href="/docs/en/server-managed-settings">server-managed settings</a>. If the fetch fails, Claude Code exits instead of continuing with cached or no settings. Set it when your environment can’t accept even a brief window in which a session runs without its managed policy.</span>
<span data-as="p">When the key is unset, Claude Code doesn’t block startup on the fetch, though when the developer signs in at startup it waits up to five seconds for the fetch. A Cloud gateway session always waits, and exits if the gateway can’t be reached.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Managed</code></a>. Claude Code honors a <code>true</code> from any admin-controlled managed source, even one that isn’t the highest-priority source.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: Boolean<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>true</code>: Claude Code blocks startup until it has freshly fetched server-managed settings, and exits if the fetch fails</li>
<li><code>false</code>: Claude Code doesn’t block startup on the fetch, though at a sign-in startup it waits up to five seconds for the fetch</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: <code>false</code></li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Set it in an MDM profile or the managed settings file to enforce fail-closed startup before the first server payload arrives. Claude Code applies the check only in sessions that fetch server-managed settings, so a session that <a class="link" href="/docs/en/server-managed-settings#platform-availability">doesn’t fetch them</a> starts without waiting. The <code>claude auth</code> subcommands are exempt, so users can re-authenticate when expired credentials are why the fetch fails. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/server-managed-settings#enforce-fail-closed-startup">Enforce fail-closed startup</a>.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="managedsourcesbehavior"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#managedsourcesbehavior">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>managedSourcesBehavior</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Choose whether Claude Code applies only the highest-priority <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#how-claude-code-combines-managed-sources">managed source</a> your organization delivers, or combines every admin source it delivers. By default Claude Code takes the highest-priority source that carries a <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#how-claude-code-combines-managed-sources">policy key</a> and ignores the rest. A policy key is any settings key other than this one and <code>wslInheritsWindowsSettings</code>. So once server-managed settings or an MDM policy deliver a policy key, a <code>managed-settings.json</code> file contributes only the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#keys-read-from-every-admin-source">keys Claude Code reads from every admin source</a>. With <code>"merge"</code>, every admin source you deliver contributes its keys to one combined policy. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.</span>
<span data-as="p">Set <code>"merge"</code> only where every source <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#how-claude-code-combines-managed-sources">ranked</a> below your highest one is under an administrator’s control, because Claude Code then adds entries from a lower source, such as <code>permissions.allow</code> rules, to the policy.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Managed</code></a>. Claude Code reads this key from the highest-priority source that carries either this key or a policy key, and ignores this key in every source ranked lower, so a lower source can’t opt itself into combining with the source above it. Neither the Windows HKCU registry nor <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#let-an-embedding-host-add-policy">parent settings from an embedding host</a> take part in the merge.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: string, one of:<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>"first-wins"</code>: the highest-priority source that carries a policy key supplies the policy, and lower sources contribute only the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#keys-read-from-every-admin-source">keys Claude Code reads from every admin source</a></li>
<li><code>"merge"</code>: every admin source you deliver contributes its keys, combined by the rules below</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: <code>"first-wins"</code></li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">Deliver the key in the highest-priority source you deploy. A machine that never receives server-managed settings needs the key in its MDM profile too, because Claude Code reads the key from the highest-priority source that carries it or a policy key. A <code>managed-settings.json</code> file is the lowest-ranked admin source, so <code>"merge"</code> set there has no source below it to combine with. In server-managed settings, the key looks like this:</span>

<span data-as="p">Under <code>"merge"</code>, Claude Code combines each key by its kind. This table gives the rule for each kind. The restriction allowlist, values-taken-whole, and highest-source-only rows name every key they cover, and the other rows give examples:</span>

When no source sets a strict value, applies a looser value only from the highest source</td><td style="text-align:left"><a class="link" href="#allowmanagedpermissionrulesonly"><code>allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly</code></a>, <a class="link" href="#permissions-disablebypasspermissionsmode"><code>permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode</code></a>, and other boolean or enum locks</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left">Restriction allowlists</td><td style="text-align:left">Takes the list whole from the highest source that sets it, without adding entries from lower sources. When the highest source doesn’t set one, takes it whole from the next source down</td><td style="text-align:left"><a class="link" href="#availablemodels"><code>availableModels</code></a>, <a class="link" href="#allowedmcpservers"><code>allowedMcpServers</code></a>, <a class="link" href="#strictknownmarketplaces"><code>strictKnownMarketplaces</code></a>, <a class="link" href="#allowedchannelplugins"><code>allowedChannelPlugins</code></a>, and the <a class="link" href="#fallbackmodel"><code>fallbackModel</code></a> chain</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left">Values taken whole</td><td style="text-align:left">Takes the value whole from the highest source that sets it, without combining entries or fields from lower sources. When the highest source doesn’t set it, takes it whole from the next source down</td><td style="text-align:left"><a class="link" href="#sandbox-credentials-awspairs"><code>sandbox.credentials.awsPairs</code></a>, <a class="link" href="#sandbox-ripgrep"><code>sandbox.ripgrep</code></a></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left">Provided MCP servers</td><td style="text-align:left">Combines the server names from every source. When two sources set the same name, applies the higher source’s whole entry</td><td style="text-align:left"><a class="link" href="#managedmcpservers"><code>managedMcpServers</code></a></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left">Read from the highest-priority source only</td><td style="text-align:left">Reads the key only from the highest-priority source that carries a policy key, so a lower source’s value is ignored even when the highest source sets none</td><td style="text-align:left"><a class="link" href="#apikeyhelper"><code>apiKeyHelper</code></a>, <a class="link" href="#awsauthrefresh"><code>awsAuthRefresh</code></a>, <a class="link" style="text-align:left">Every other key</td><td style="text-align:left">Takes the value from the highest source that sets it</td><td style="text-align:left"><a class="link" href="#cleanupperioddays"><code>cleanupPeriodDays</code></a>, <a class="link" href="#model"><code>model</code></a></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>
<span data-as="p">Taking <code>sandbox.credentials.awsPairs</code> and <code>sandbox.ripgrep</code> whole requires Claude Code v2.1.257 or later.</span>
<span data-as="p">Three of those keys add a condition of their own:</span>
<ul>
<li><strong><a class="link" href="#policyhelper"><code>policyHelper</code></a></strong>: Claude Code honors it only when the highest source that carries a policy key is an MDM policy or a managed settings file, so under server-managed settings it doesn’t apply.</li>
<li><strong><a class="link" href="#modeloverrides"><code>modelOverrides</code></a></strong>: pairs with <code>availableModels</code>. Claude Code takes <code>modelOverrides</code> from the highest source that sets it, unless a higher source sets <code>availableModels</code> without <code>modelOverrides</code>. In that case it ignores <code>modelOverrides</code> from every source.</li>
<li><strong><a class="link" href="#forcelogingatewayurl"><code>forceLoginGatewayUrl</code></a> and the <code>"gateway"</code> value of <a class="link" href="#forceloginmethod"><code>forceLoginMethod</code></a></strong>: Claude Code reads them only from the managed sources on the machine itself and ignores them in server-managed settings. The machine’s values apply even when server-managed settings are also present.</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">To confirm which sources combined on a machine, run <code>/status</code> and <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#read-the-source-in-/status">read the <code>Setting sources</code> line</a>.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="parentsettingsbehavior"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#parentsettingsbehavior">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>parentSettingsBehavior</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Choose whether Claude Code applies managed settings supplied by an embedding host process, such as the Agent SDK or an IDE extension, when an admin-deployed managed tier is also present. With <code>"first-wins"</code>, Claude Code drops the host-supplied settings; with <code>"merge"</code>, it applies them under the admin tier through a restrictive-only filter. Set <code>"merge"</code> when a host needs to pass its own restrictions to the sessions it launches, for example Claude Desktop delivering a gateway’s egress allowlist.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Managed</code></a>. Claude Code reads it from the highest-priority admin-controlled managed source.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: string, one of:<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>"first-wins"</code>: Claude Code drops the host-supplied settings when an admin-deployed managed tier is present</li>
<li><code>"merge"</code>: Claude Code applies the host-supplied settings under the admin tier through a restrictive-only filter</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: <code>"first-wins"</code></li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">This key has no effect when no admin-deployed managed tier exists: the host’s settings then apply as the only managed tier, still filtered to restrictive values. For the filter’s limits and how the managed sources interact, see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#parent-settings-from-embedding-hosts">Parent settings from embedding hosts</a> and <a class="link" href="/docs/en/claude-apps-gateway#restrict-parent-settings">Restrict parent settings</a>.</span>
<span id="compute-managed-settings-with-a-policy-helper"></span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="policyhelper"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#policyhelper">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>policyHelper</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Run an executable you deploy that computes managed settings at startup, so you can derive policy from device posture, identity, or a remote service instead of a static file. Claude Code runs the helper before it accepts the first prompt and treats the settings it emits as the managed settings for the session.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Managed</code></a>. Read from the macOS plist, the Windows HKLM registry, or the managed settings file. Claude Code reads the key from the highest-priority managed source that carries a <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#how-claude-code-combines-managed-sources">policy key</a> and runs the helper only when that source is one of those three; it ignores the key in server-managed settings, the HKCU registry, and host-supplied parent settings.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: object with <code>path</code>, <code>timeoutMs</code>, and <code>refreshIntervalMs</code></li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so no helper runs</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">When server-managed settings deliver the policy at launch, they take precedence over the helper’s source and the helper doesn’t run.</span>
<span data-as="p">If a later settings fetch reports the server-managed settings removed, Claude Code runs the helper at that point rather than waiting for the next launch. Its output governs the rest of the session, and a run that fails ends the session with the same message as a <a class="link" href="#helper-failures">failed startup run</a>.</span>
<span data-as="p">This example runs the helper with a 5-second timeout and re-runs it every five minutes:</span>

</code></pre></div></div></div></div><div aria-hidden="true" class="code-block-fade-overlay print:hidden" data-fade-overlay="true" style="--fade-color-light:#ffffff;--fade-color-dark:#0B0C0E"></div></div>
<span data-as="p">When the helper emits <code>managedSettings</code>, that object becomes the only managed settings source for the run: Claude Code ignores the MDM, file, and HKCU sources, reads the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#keys-read-from-every-admin-source">cross-source keys</a> from the helper’s output alone, and never merges <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#parent-settings-from-embedding-hosts">parent settings</a>.</span>
<span data-as="p">The startup <code>forceRemoteSettingsRefresh</code> check runs before the helper and reads any admin source. A helper that exits <code>0</code> with an envelope that omits <code>managedSettings</code> contributes no managed settings, and the other sources apply as usual.</span>
<h4 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="helper-failures"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#helper-failures">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Helper failures</span></h4>
<span data-as="p">A helper run fails when:</span>
<ul>
<li><code>path</code> breaks the rules in <a class="link" href="#policyhelper-path"><code>policyHelper.path</code></a>.</li>
<li>No regular file is at <code>path</code>. Claude Code checks for the file before starting the helper, within the same <code>timeoutMs</code> budget, so an unresponsive network mount can cause the run to fail.</li>
<li>The helper exits non-zero, is still running when <code>timeoutMs</code> elapses, or doesn’t start at all, for example because it isn’t executable.</li>
<li>The helper writes more than 1 MiB to stdout or to stderr.</li>
<li>stdout isn’t a single JSON object, or its <code>managedSettings</code> has a <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#find-entries-claude-code-dropped">schema violation Claude Code can’t repair</a>.</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">When the startup run fails, Claude Code prints the reason and refuses to start. After a non-zero exit or a timeout, the message includes the helper’s stderr. The refusal covers interactive sessions, <code>claude -p</code>, Agent SDK sessions, <a class="link" href="/docs/en/agent-view">background sessions</a>, and most subcommands.</span>
<span data-as="p">The refusal is deliberate, so a helper that needs outage resilience should serve from its own cache and exit <code>0</code>.</span>
<span data-as="p">When a background refresh fails, Claude Code keeps the last successful policy in effect, and <code>/status</code> shows the failing refresh with its reason until a refresh succeeds. Each refresh runs under the same <code>timeoutMs</code> and failure rules as the startup run.</span>
<span data-as="p">With <code>--debug</code>, Claude Code writes the helper’s stderr from every run to the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/debug-your-config">debug log</a>.</span>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code reports an invalid <code>policyHelper</code> value as a <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#find-entries-claude-code-dropped">dropped entry</a> and starts the session on the remaining managed settings without running a helper. Invalid values include a bare path string and a <code>timeoutMs</code> below <a class="link" href="#policyhelper-timeoutms">its minimum</a>.</span>
<span data-as="p">To turn a helper off, remove the key from the source that sets it.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="policyhelper-path"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#policyhelper-path">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>policyHelper.path</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Name the helper executable Claude Code runs. For what happens when the path breaks the rules below, see <a class="link" href="#helper-failures">Helper failures</a>.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Managed</code></a>. Read from the macOS plist, the Windows HKLM registry, or the managed settings file, wherever <a class="link" href="#policyhelper"><code>policyHelper</code></a> is read.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: string, an absolute path in normalized form, without <code>.</code> or <code>..</code> segments; on Windows, a drive-letter or UNC path that ends in <code>.exe</code></li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: none; required when <code>policyHelper</code> is set</li>
</ul>

<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="policyhelper-timeoutms"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a aria-label="Navigate to header" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" href="#policyhelper-timeoutms">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0" fill="none" height="18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-width="2" viewbox="0 0 18 18" width="18" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" linecap="round" linejoin="round" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="min-w-0 break-words cursor-pointer"><code>policyHelper.timeoutMs</code></span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Set how long Claude Code waits for the helper before treating the run as failed. A timed-out run fails the same way as a non-zero exit, so at startup Claude Code refuses to start.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Managed</code></a>. Read from the macOS plist, the Windows HKLM registry, or the managed settings file, wherever <a class="link" href="#policyhelper"><code>policyHelper</code></a> is read.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: integer, milliseconds, minimum <code>1000</code></li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: <code>10000</code></li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Have Claude Code re-run the helper in the background on an interval so policy changes reach a running session. When a refresh succeeds, its output replaces the previous managed settings without a restart; when a refresh fails, Claude Code keeps the policy it already has.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Managed</code></a>. Read from the macOS plist, the Windows HKLM registry, or the managed settings file, wherever <a class="link" href="#policyhelper"><code>policyHelper</code></a> is read.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: integer, milliseconds: <code>0</code> to disable refresh, otherwise at least <code>60000</code></li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: unset, so Claude Code runs the helper once at startup</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">This example re-runs the helper every five minutes:</span>

<span data-as="p">Have Claude Code on WSL read managed settings from the Windows policy chain, with HKLM and the Windows managed settings file taking priority over <code>/etc/claude-code</code> and HKCU below it. While the chain is on, Claude Code reads <code>/etc/claude-code</code> only when no managed settings file or drop-in under <code>C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\</code> delivers a <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#how-claude-code-combines-managed-sources">policy key</a>. Set it to extend the policy you already deploy on Windows to WSL sessions on the same machine, so they follow the same rules as host sessions. Claude Code honors it only when set in the HKLM registry key or in a managed settings file or drop-in under <code>C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\</code>, both of which require Windows admin to write.</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Scope</strong>: <a class="link" href="#scopes"><code>Managed</code></a>. In an admin-controlled Windows source.</li>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: Boolean<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>true</code>: Claude Code on WSL reads managed settings from the Windows policy chain, and reads <code>/etc/claude-code</code> only when no managed settings file or drop-in under <code>C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\</code> delivers a <a class="link" href="/docs/en/managed-settings#how-claude-code-combines-managed-sources">policy key</a></li>
<li><code>false</code>: WSL reads only <code>/etc/claude-code</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Default</strong>: <code>false</code>, so WSL reads only <code>/etc/claude-code</code></li>
</ul>
